en.1: This is our second time with Harry Potter.
en.2: Let's just go through three pages together again today.
en.4: Before we start, let's quickly look back at what we learned last time.
en.5: Remember Mrs. Dursley craning her neck to peer over the fence, straining to see into the neighbors' gardens?
en.6: Just recall that for a second, and today will go a lot easier.
en.8: People on the street are staring up at the sky, mouths hanging open.
en.11: Because a whole crowd of owls is swooping overhead — in broad daylight.
en.12: That swooping feeling — the author catches it with the word swoop.
en.13: You can just picture wings spreading and diving straight down, right?
en.14: But Mr. Dursley is the only one who doesn't see any of it.
en.15: It says he had a very normal, owl-free morning — and there's something cute about that phrasing.
en.17: Just one word tacked on, used almost like a little joke.
en.18: This is the heart of today's lesson.
en.19: Passing by the bakery at lunchtime, he catches a few whispered words from some people in cloaks.
en.21: Here the author doesn't write 'heard' — she writes catch.
en.22: It's not just something that drifted past his ears — you know how, even in a noisy place, the one thing about you, the thing you care about, just jumps out at you?
en.25: And the moment he hears that name, Mr. Dursley freezes, dead still.
en.27: This rushing over — that's the very word flood.
en.28: For a man who's such a control freak, 'flood' — what a powerless word to use.
en.29: He starts dialing his wife's number, nearly finishes it, then stops — no, never mind — and sets the receiver back down.
en.30: Trying hard to tell himself it's nothing, that it's a common name.
en.31: Back at the office, he can't get anything done.
en.32: But the author doesn't write 'couldn't concentrate' — she uses find.
en.33: He found that concentrating was a good deal harder than usual.
en.34: He's realizing it himself — his own mind isn't listening to him.
en.35: Find — she uses it a lot for that feeling of discovering something through experience.
en.36: On his way home, he bumps into a strange old man in a purple cloak, who, instead of getting angry, breaks into a huge grin and throws his arms around Mr. Dursley.
en.37: That feeling of real dismay, being shaken up like something rattling — that's rattled.
en.39: The old man in the purple cloak hugs Mr. Dursley and says this.
en.41: Called a Muggle — a word he doesn't even know — by a total stranger, and hugged by him.
en.42: His perfect, ordinary day is falling apart just like that.
en.44: Who on earth is this old man?
en.46: In the next part, once night falls, the real magic begins.
en.47: Whether you're here for the first time today, or you've been reading along for a while, or you're back after a few days off — welcome, all of you.
en.48: Just making it this far is enough.
en.51: This is Stella, see you again tomorrow.
